thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: elevated error rate and correctness regressions observed for inference requests matching prefix `org:tenant-123/*` in eu-west-1. Error spike started ~02:12 UTC. Paging oncall (devon) and eng-runtime. Logs: increased 500s and KV-cache bypasses.

devon: acked. I'm oncall. quick ask: is this correctness-only (stale cache) or load-induced? any P50/P95 changes?

mike_r: P95 latency up ~2.2x for that prefix, errors are mainly `kv_cache_miss -> downstream fetch -> parity-fail`. Looks like some KV entries returning older model-version keys. Not a pure load spike.

helena: seeing traffic skew to a small set of hot prefixes tied to onboarding flow. 3 tenants hit, primary is tenant-123 (payment flows). severity: potentially customer-facing incorrect outputs. Recommend immediate cache-bypass for correctness on critical routes, and soft rate-limit on regen to reduce downstream churn.

devon: agree. plan: 1) apply per-tenant cache-bypass for `tenant-123` on correctness path (no prefix prefetch). 2) apply temporary rate-limit to 30 rps for that tenant's generate route, 3) route traffic fallback to model-variant v1.2-safe for that tenant if errors persist. Anyone object?

chris: +1. I'll run the config change and monitor.

sara_ops: tagging support - customer-impact note: tenant-123 has 2 live customers on prod (acme-payroll, beta-payments). We'll prep comms if we switch to degraded mode.

mike_r: posting current quick metrics:
- error-rate tenant-123 /v1/generate: 12% -> 28% spike on 02:12
- tokens/sec: steady, but backend fetches up 3x
- kv-prefetch failure rate: 18%

chris: executing mitigation steps now.

chris: command applied to control plane:
```bash
# disable prefix prefetch for tenant-123 correctness path
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.internal/api/v1/tenants/tenant-123/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"cache": {"prefix_prefetch_enabled": false, "kv_bypass_on_correctness": true}}'
```

incident-bot: Deployment event: control-plane config change triggered by chris at 02:24 UTC. ID: cfg-1794123499.

chris: also applying soft rate cap via traffic-shaper: set `generate` route to 30 rps for tenant-123, burst 10. Command:
```json
{"tenant":"tenant-123","route":"/v1/generate","rate_limit":{"rps":30,"burst":10}}
```

devon: good. increase logging verbosity for that tenant to capture first two failed responses per session.

mike_r: logs show immediate drop in downstream fetch retries from 3 -> 1 per request. error-rate down to 7% at 02:32. latency P95 back to 1.3x baseline.

helena: re: customer impact - acme-payroll reported a small number of anomalous outputs earlier, but appears stable now. Recommend keeping cache-bypass (correctness path) for 2 hours, keep rate-limit for 1 hour, then re-evaluate.

devon: agree. I'll open an incident checklist and set next actions.

devon: ACTIONS:
- [ ] Keep `kv_bypass_on_correctness` for tenant-123 for 2h (chris)
- [ ] Maintain 30 rps rate cap for 1h (chris)
- [ ] Run cache-integrity rollback test against a sample of keys (mike_r)
- [ ] Prepare customer note if switching to fallback model (sara_ops)

chris: marking config sticky for 2h via control-plane.

incident-bot: Note: automatic quota autoscale suspended for tenant-123 to avoid accidental capacity increases during mitigation.

mike_r: running quick integrity test: sampling 200 keys under prefix `tenant-123/session/*` to compare KV versions vs model-serving metadata. will post results.

mike_r: test results: 200/200 matched expected latest versions after bypass; indicates stale prefetch was causative.

devon: nice. recommend also adding a short-term traffic split so new writes bypass the prefetch path entirely while we run deeper diagnostics. Set split: 90% direct bypass, 10% prefetch (for metrics).

chris: applying traffic-split:
```yaml
- name: tenant-123-prefetch-split
  match: prefix("tenant-123/")
  actions:
    - route: bypass-prefetch
      pct: 90
    - route: prefetch
      pct: 10
```

incident-bot: traffic-split applied at 02:46 UTC.

sara_ops: customer impact update: acme-payroll sees normal behavior now. They're monitoring. No escalations.

helena: I'm taking handover at 04:00 UTC. devon will remain available if needed. Leaving notes in the incident doc: reason = stale prefix prefetch; mitigation = cache-bypass + rate-limit + traffic-split.

devon: handing off to helena for monitoring window. If error-rate stays <5% for 30m and integrity tests hold, we'll roll prefetch re-enable as a canary at 1% traffic.

helena: ack. I'll coordinate the canary re-enable and let support know.

incident-bot: Monitoring: error-rate steady at 3.8% for 20m; latency close to baseline. Next automated check at 03:30 UTC.

mike_r: prepping follow-up: deeper root-cause ticket to eng-runtime to investigate race between KV-refresh and model-version migration, include reproducer + timeline.

helena: confirmed - set reminder to re-evaluate at 05:00 UTC. turning on lightweight alerting for key prefixes.

devon: marking incident as mitigated. leaving open until postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident mitigated by config changes. Keeping thread open for postmortem notes.
